newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Ousted Indonesia party leader debuts on web.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Indonesia party leader debuts on web.

text.p: Ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, blocked by the government from contesting the country's May 29 election, now has a homepage on the Internet's world wide web.

Creators of the Indonesian-language "Merah Putih Online" (www.merahputih.com), which opened this week, said the page will be updated with a weekly interview and twice-weekly Megawati editorials and other articles. The frequency of updates would increase as the May 29 polls draw nearer, they said.
Merah Putih means red and white, the colours of the Indonesian flag.
"We need Merah Putih to clarify what Megawati's views are as there is a lot of wrong information about her out there," said one of the homepage's creators, who asked not to be identified.

The government and military regularly pressure Indonesia's newspaper editors to restrict or censor news about Megawati, who was deposed as head of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) during a government-backed congress last June.
Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's first president Sukarno, remains popular and draws large crowds in her travels around the country.
"She still has the right to express her views and give her opinions as she is still a member of parliament," one of the homepage's creators said on Thursday.
Commercial market research completed in December estimated more than 180,000 Indonesians in five major cities had accessed the Internet, with 85,000 having done so in the past month.
Internet access remains unregulated in Indonesia.
